1

Details

Question (Stephan, 2026-10-19): the early July running had other targets in the beam; the B4C night ran with the scintillator trigger, so could it give pairs?

Answer: no. This note shows the data that exist, the Geant4 expectation, and the reason, and compares with the ³He running.

Built by nTof_x17/ntof_b4c_target/make_b4c_deck.py from expect.json and deck_data.json (/media/dylan/data/x17/b4c_target/).

2

Details

Geometry as in MX17_Full_Geant (July survey): Micromegas front face 25 cm from the beam axis, SiPM wall behind it, the liquid-scintillator vessel, then two 2 cm plastic bars. The layer radii drawn are rounded.

The trigger in run_39/40 was N1081B mode 3: Singles (any one leg) OR Doubles (two legs), gated 30 ms after the PS pulse. A "pair event" in this note is two legs in two arms with charge in both of those arms' chambers.

Thresholds used in the simulation are the production ones (SiPM 0.5 MIP, plastic 0.9 MIP; MIP = 0.475 / 3.349 MeV from the 2 cm calibration run). In run_39 the wall thresholds were re-tuned through the night and the plastics sat at −15 mV until 09:04; slide 10 scans the plastic threshold.

run_38 (22:12–01:09) is a flash-trigger HV scan with no scintillator trigger; its run_config still says “Marex” because the target field was only corrected at 05:08. Nothing ran 01:09–05:05.

run_39: 10 × 24 min, 05:06–09:03, all chambers 560 → 530 V, drift 800 V, 32 × 60 ns. run_40: 2 sub-runs on EOS at 545 V, 09:13–09:59 (the logbook says it ran to midday; three sub-runs are missing). Beam: 2635 pulses, 2.175×10¹⁶ protons (8.25×10¹² per pulse). n_TOF DAQ runs 224451–224455 recorded the walls, plastics and liquids over the window.

The Marex period has more scintillator-triggered data (runs 32/33/36/37), but with the mesh-injection circuits on, half the trigger on liquid scintillators, and an unknown target that may have missed the beam.

4

Details

Census: ntof_b4c_target/lxplus/data_activity_census.py on EOS combined_hits_root; log copied to ntof_b4c_target/data/activity_census.log. A chamber is “active” when both its x FEU and its y FEU have 2–40 hits with amplitude > 500 ADC peaking in samples 6–28 (B4C/Marex, 32-sample window) or 0–19 (run_79, 20-sample window).

run_37 “mesh on” sub-runs show a B–C excess that looks like charge injection, not physics; run_37 sub-runs with fewer than 1000 triggers are not drawn. Chamber D was noisy in run_39 (~120 D-x hits per event against 55 in run_79), so pairs involving D are inflated.

Totals: B4C 2,300 of 71,085 triggers (3.2 %); run_79 2.4 %. About one production hour of multi-chamber candidates in total.

Details

MX17_Full_Geant branch merged to main (--slab B4C:2.5 --slab-radius R, --bias-slab, cascade entries in --gamma-lines). Three sets per disc radius (Ø100, Ø50 mm): 2×10⁷ analog beam neutrons (photon evaporation on; events with a slab ¹⁰B(n,γ) removed), 10⁷ EGAF cascades from the slab capture vertices, and 10⁶ Born IPC pairs per line. Outputs: /eos/experiment/ntof/data/x17/full_sim/b4c_july/.

The 6.740 MeV line is E2; the generator has no E2, so it uses the E2 coefficient with M1 kinematics. The 2.297 MeV line (4×10⁻⁵ pairs per capture) is left out. ¹¹B(n,γ)¹²B (3.37 MeV, 7 % of the (n,γ)) and the ¹²B β decay are not simulated.

Geant4’s ¹⁰B(n,γ) is wrong, so the measured cascade is generated

363 biased captures in the B4C disc, Geant4 11.2.1, two capture models vs the EGAF thermal-capture data

measured, EGAF (what the sim emits)

6

Details

Default ParticleHP samples the ¹⁰B capture γ lines independently from the evaluated data, so a capture can emit two 11.45 MeV γs and three 7 MeV γs at once. /process/had/particle_hp/use_photo_evaporation true conserves energy but chooses primaries from a statistical model: a third of its cascades go through a 2.12 MeV level that the thermal-capture data do not show.

The simulation therefore emits the EGAF scheme (TUNL compilation; per 100 captures): 7.007+4.444 (54.2), 4.711+6.740 (17.4), 4.711+2.297+4.444 (8.3), 2.533+8.917 (13.0), 2.533+4.475+4.444 (0.8), 11.448 (4.64), each γ isotropic from a vertex drawn from the slab captures of the neutron run. The 4.444 line then comes out at 63 % (EGAF 64.6 %).

Also from this check: Geant4 emits the 478 keV ⁷Li* line in 56 % of (n,α) (1449 of 2583) instead of 94 %. It cannot make a pair, but it sets the wall and chamber singles rates.

Source: 3000 beam neutrons with --bias-slab 1000 and /tracking/verbose 1, parsed by parse_trk2.py; ntof_b4c_target/data/{hp3k,pe3k}.json.

B4C makes 17,924× more pairs than ³He(n,γ), and loses almost all of them

Internal pairs per nominal pulse at each step of the selection, Geant4 (Ø100 mm disc; ³He capsule, same geometry)

B4C disc: ¹⁰B(n,γ) internal pairs

³He capsule: ³He(n,γ) 20.6 MeV M1 internal pairs

7

Details

B4C: 1.62 pairs per pulse made; 0.115 with the e⁺ and e⁻ in two different chambers; 8.61e-06 with two trigger legs; 8.54e-06 with two legs and charge in both leg chambers. Over the exposure (3107 nominal pulses) that is 0.027 events. Ø50 mm gives the same within MC error.

³He: 44.8 % of beam neutrons are absorbed in the gas ((n,p), current EAR2 profile run neutrons_thermal_ear2_L19p5), ³He(n,γ)/(n,p) = 55 µb / 5333 b, α(M1, 20.58 MeV) = 3.66×10⁻³: 9.0e-05 pairs per pulse. Per pair: two legs + both chambers 1.71e-03 (M1), 6.60e-03 (E0), 9.63e-03 (X17). The ³He pair runs: 2×10⁵ each, vertices from the capsule gas library, same build and thresholds.

Even with more pairs surviving per pulse than ³He(n,γ), B4C stays far below one event: the thermal gate is not where either target’s pair physics is visible.

8

Details

A lepton must cross the Micromegas, the SiPM wall and the liquid-scintillator vessel (2.6 mm CFRP plus ~2 cm of LAB) and still leave 3.0 MeV (0.9 MIP) in a 2 cm plastic bar. That takes roughly ≥ 8–10 MeV of kinetic energy at normal incidence. A pair from a W MeV transition shares W − 1.02 MeV between its two leptons, so below ~10 MeV at most one of them can make it.

Only the 11.448 MeV ground-state line (4.6 % of captures) ever gives a two-leg pair. ³He E0 and X17 pairs are more open than M1, so more of them split over two arms.

The ³He capsule’s aluminium already makes more of these pairs than the B4C did

Internal pairs made and passing per nominal pulse: the B4C night against the ³He running in the 1–30 ms gate

pairs made

pairs that pass (lighter)

Per pulse, the ³He capsule’s own aluminium makes 24× more few-MeV pairs than the B4C disc did, through the whole production run.

So the B4C night adds nothing the ³He data lack: both see these low-energy pairs equally poorly.

The ³He physics is the 20.6 MeV line, which the trigger was built for — and only in the MeV window is it frequent enough to show.

9

Details

³He(n,γ): 0.025 captures per pulse in the gas, 9.0e-05 M1 internal pairs. The E0 channel is not bounded by the (n,γ) cross section (CLAUDE.md conventions, ipc_born); it is left out of the bar.

Capsule Al: 15,160 captures per pulse (He3Cap_Al, 0.285 % of beam neutrons, analog run neutrons_thermal_ear2_L19p5), × Σ I·α = 2.56×10⁻³ over the ²⁸Al lines above 2 MeV, all taken as E1: 39 pairs per pulse. Approximate (secondary lines are not all E1), but the order of magnitude is the point.

External conversion is not in these bars. It is larger than IPC for both targets (in the capsule, 84.5 % of the capsule pairs reaching a drift gap are Al external conversions — CAMPAIGN_STATUS 2026-09-15), and it has the same energy problem.

No plastic threshold rescues it

Two-arm (Doubles) events from the disc over the whole exposure, against the plastic threshold

¹⁰B(n,γ) cascade γs (two arms, Compton)

¹⁰B(n,γ) internal pairs

10

Details

The run_39 thresholds moved during the night: the wall (M1) thresholds were tuned 05:06–09:01 (A 30 → 20 mV, B 45 → 55 mV, then up to 133–160 mV), and the plastics (M2) stayed at −15 mV until 09:04, when they went to −65/−80 mV. The pre-FIFO −15 mV is roughly the production 0.9 MIP (the 17 July fan-out doubled the amplitude and the threshold went to −30 mV). This scan covers that whole range.

The beam-neutron source gives no Doubles at any threshold (no MC events in 2×10⁷ neutrons). Doubles from the cascade γs are two Compton electrons in two arms, not pairs.

What this does not rule out

The chamber occupancy does not match. Geant4 lights each chamber ~1900 times per pulse (Compton electrons from the 478 keV ⁷Li line), which would put two chambers in almost every readout. The data show a few %, as in production. The data criterion is much harder than a 3 keV deposit, so this is open; it could also mean the disc was small or off axis (the May test found it misaligned).

The target itself is undocumented: diameter, density (2.52 g/cm³ assumed), position along the beam, and “2.5 mm, I think?”. None of these changes the verdict: the pairs are lost at the plastics, not at the target.

Not simulated: room-return and epithermal neutrons, the flash and 0–1 ms, accidental coincidences between captures, ¹¹B(n,γ) and the ¹²B β decay, E2 kinematics for the 6.74 MeV line.

What it does say: any low-energy pair source in the thermal gate — B4C, or the capsule’s own aluminium — is invisible to this trigger. The early-July targets offer no pair sample beyond what the ³He production data already contain.
